title: Seven-round AES-128 single-key MITM key recovery, low-memory tradeoff

target.description: Seven-round AES-128 under the author's zero-based round numbering, rounds 0 through 6, with the real AES key schedule and the reduced cipher's final MixColumns omitted.

setting.key_relation: One unknown secret key; no related-key oracle is assumed.
setting.key_population: general secret key; no weak-key restriction reported
setting.plaintext_model: chosen-plaintext structures under one secret key
assumptions: Chosen-plaintext structures and the source's truncated-differential analysis.
Precomputed multiset tables and the source's AES-encryption-equivalent cost model.

time.note: Author-reported AES-encryption-equivalent time; the optimized tradeoff's preprocessing is not separately itemized, so this is not asserted to be an independently checked total offline-plus-online budget. Section3.3quotes key-testing work rather than establishing an oracle-inclusive total: the D105endpoint exceeds itsT99quote, unlike the simple Section3.2accounting.

data.note: Chosen plaintexts used by the Section 3.3 data-memory tradeoff; not known plaintexts or decryption queries.

memory.note: Multiset-table storage measured in 128-bit AES blocks, following Section 2.1 and Section 3.3.

preprocessing.note: Precomputed tables are required, but a separate preprocessing budget for this optimized tradeoff is not extracted; missing does not mean zero.

success.description: The efficient attack uses2^105 chosen plaintexts to expect one conforming pair at time2^99 and memory2^90. Section3.4 explicitly recovers the final two round keys by extracting table parameters and repeating smaller DS checks at negligible extra work. The missing success ingredient is the finite-data pair-acquisition and joint output law, not absence of a completion construction.

review.scope: Exact Sections3.3–3.4 assignment checked independently. The two-last-subkey completion is positively evidenced; expected one useful pair is not converted into certainty or1-exp(-1). The2^97-data/2^98-memory parallel-table row remains separate. Primary success stays unquantified; no new full-paper audit.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.4-5, Section 2.1, round conventions and resource units; p.8, Table 1, AES-128 7-round row with data 2^105; p.12, Section 3.3, first efficient attack; p.13, Section 3.4, key recovery.
evidence.interpretation: The authors report time 2^99, data 2^105 chosen plaintexts and memory 2^90 AES blocks before the additional multiple-table data reduction. Section 3.4 supplies complete secret-key recovery. This is an attack construction, not a security lower bound; unreported numerical success and separate preprocessing remain null.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.1–17 complete read; p.5native units; pp.10–13 seven-round costs and completion; pp.14–16 schedule-dependent extensions.
evidence.interpretation: Raw-first independent full inventory, original-PDF SHA recheck, bounded official version/successor checks. Existing quoted resource tuple and stableIDpreserved; no author code executed.

evidence.locator: PDF8 Table1; PDF10–13 Sections3.2–3.4 and complete-key completion paragraph.
evidence.interpretation: Targeted success audit: expected counts and conditional correctness are retained without inventing an end-to-end probability or a Poisson independence assumption.

evidence.locator: Author PDF11–13 Section3.3, Figure4,2^105-data/2^99-time/2^90-memory assignment and separate parallel-table tradeoff; PDF13 Section3.4 complete two-last-subkey recovery.
evidence.interpretation: The paper supplies an explicit budget-compatible key-completion construction. It does not give a numerical probability that the finite plaintext structures contain a suitable pair or a joint completed-key success rate.

limitations: The attack, multiset tables and reported costs have not been independently executed or reproduced.
Unknown numerical success and separate preprocessing prevent automatic frontier comparison, including with the companion AES-128 tradeoff.
